'''Bridgeport''' is the [[List of municipalities in Connecticut|most populous city]] in the U.S. state of [[Connecticut]].<ref>{{cite web |title = Annual Town and County Population for Connecticut |url = https://portal.ct.gov/DPH/Health-Information-Systems--Reporting/Population/Annual-Town-and-County-Population-for-Connecticut |website = portal.ct.gov |access-date = May 22, 2020 |archive-date = May 19, 2020 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200519035145/https://portal.ct.gov/DPH/Health-Information-Systems--Reporting/Population/Annual-Town-and-County-Population-for-Connecticut |url-status = live }}</ref> The population was 148,654 in 2020, making it the [[List of cities in New England by population|fifth-most populous city in New England]].<ref name="USCensus2020"/> It is a port city in eastern [[Fairfield County, Connecticut|Fairfield County]] at the mouth of the [[Pequonnock River]] on [[Long Island Sound]], {{Convert|60|mi|km|abbr=out}} from [[Manhattan]] and {{Convert|40|mi|km|abbr=out}} from [[The Bronx]]. Bridgeport and other towns in Fairfield County make up the [[Greater Bridgeport Planning Region, Connecticut|Greater Bridgeport Planning Region]], as well as the [[Greater Bridgeport|Bridgeport–Stamford–Norwalk–Danbury metropolitan statistical area]], the second largest metropolitan area in Connecticut and a component of the greater [[New York metropolitan area]].

Inhabited by the [[Golden Hill Paugussett Indian Nation|Paugussett]] Native American tribe until English colonisation in the 1600s, Bridgeport was incorporated as a town in 1821 and as a city in 1836. Showman [[P. T. Barnum]] was a resident of the city and served as the town's mayor in 1871.<ref>{{cite web |title=10 Things You May Not Know About P.T. Barnum |url=https://www.history.com/news/10-things-you-may-not-know-about-p-t-barnum |last=Andrews |first=Evan |website=HISTORY |date=July 2, 2015 |language=en |access-date=May 22, 2020 |archive-date=May 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200529144901/https://www.history.com/news/10-things-you-may-not-know-about-p-t-barnum |url-status=live }}</ref> Barnum built four houses in Bridgeport and housed his [[Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus|circus]] in town during winter. In the early 20th century, the city saw an economic and population boom, becoming by all measures Connecticut's chief [[industrial city|manufacturing city]] by 1905.<ref name="EB1911">{{cite EB1911 |wstitle=Bridgeport |volume=3 |page=532}}</ref>

Bridgeport was the site of the world's first [[Telephone exchange|mutual telephone exchange]] (1877),<ref name="Popular Science">{{cite magazine |first=Fred |last=De Land |date=December 1906 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tiUDAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA498 |title=Notes on the Development of Telephone Service |magazine=Popular Science Monthly |page=498 |access-date=July 31, 2022 |via=Google Books |archive-date=September 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230930093059/https://books.google.com/books?id=tiUDAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA498#v=onepage&q&f=false |url-status=live }}</ref> the first [[Dental hygienist|dental hygiene]] [[University of Bridgeport|school]] (1949),<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bridgeport.edu/academics/schools-colleges/fones-school-dental-hygiene/ |title=Dental Hygiene School in CT | University of Bridgeport |access-date=July 11, 2022 |archive-date=July 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704143140/https://www.bridgeport.edu/academics/schools-colleges/fones-school-dental-hygiene/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and the first [[People's United Financial|bank telephone bill service in the US]] (1981).<ref>Only in Bridgeport, a History of the Park City: Lenne Grimaldi</ref> Inventor [[Harvey Hubbell]] II invented the first American [[AC power plugs and sockets|electric plug outlet]] in Bridgeport in 1912.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://connecticuthistory.org/first-us-detachable-electric-plug-today-in-history-november-8/ |title=First US Detachable Electric Plug – Today in History: November 8 - Connecticut History | a CTHumanities Project |date=November 8, 2020 |access-date=July 29, 2022 |archive-date=September 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929201323/https://connecticuthistory.org/first-us-detachable-electric-plug-today-in-history-november-8/ |url-status=live }}</ref>{{Failed verification|date=June 2026}} The [[Frisbie Pie Company]] was founded and operated in Bridgeport.<ref>{{cite web |title=History Of Frisbies |url=http://bridgeport.ct.schoolwebpages.com/education/components/scrapbook/default.php?sectiondetailid=26565 |access-date=November 28, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071110233617/http://bridgeport.ct.schoolwebpages.com/education/components/scrapbook/default.php?sectiondetailid=26565 |archive-date=November 10, 2007 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The world's first [[Subway (restaurant)|Subway]] restaurant opened in the city's North End in 1965.<ref>{{cite book |author=Emily Ross, Angus Holland |title=One hundred great businesses and the minds behind them |year=2005 |publisher=Sourcebooks, Inc. |page=388 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6qSx2UrQ_H0C&pg=PA388 |isbn=978-1-4022-0631-3}}</ref> After [[World War II]], industrial decline and [[suburbanization]] led to the loss of major employers and affluent residents, contributing to poverty and violent crime.<ref name="auto4">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1985/10/13/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-of-living-in-bridgeport.html |title=If You're Thinking of Living in; Bridgeport |newspaper=The New York Times |date=October 13, 1985 |last1=Magubane |first1=Vukani |access-date=July 6, 2022 |archive-date=July 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706192322/https://www.nytimes.com/1985/10/13/realestate/if-you-re-thinking-of-living-in-bridgeport.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Since the early 21st century, however, the city has undertaken significant redevelopment efforts, and its crime rate fell by nearly 50 percent between 2010 and 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.macrotrends.net/cities/us/ct/bridgeport/crime-rate-statistics |title=Bridgeport CT Crime Rate 2004-2018 |access-date=December 9, 2022 |archive-date=December 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205184708/https://www.macrotrends.net/cities/us/ct/bridgeport/crime-rate-statistics |url-status=live }}</ref>

Bridgeport is home to [[List of museums in Connecticut|three museums]];<ref name="auto3">{{cite web |url=https://www.shudiscovery.org/about/history/ |title=History – SHU Discovery Science Center |access-date=July 3, 2022 |archive-date=August 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813021716/https://www.shudiscovery.org/about/history/ |url-status=live }}</ref> the [[University of Bridgeport]], [[Housatonic Community College]], and part of [[Sacred Heart University]];<ref>{{cite web |url=https://barnum-museum.org/about/about-the-museum/ |title=About the Museum |access-date=July 3, 2022 |archive-date=July 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703130208/https://barnum-museum.org/about/about-the-museum/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sacredheart.edu/news-room/news-listing/sacred-heart-and-university-of-bridgeport/ |title=Sacred Heart and University of Bridgeport |date=June 30, 2020 |access-date=July 3, 2022 |archive-date=November 16, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116051249/https://www.sacredheart.edu/news-room/news-listing/sacred-heart-and-university-of-bridgeport/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and the [[Connecticut's Beardsley Zoo|state's only zoo]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.beardsleyzoo.org/about.html |title=About |access-date=July 3, 2022 |archive-date=July 12, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220712042824/https://www.beardsleyzoo.org/about.html |url-status=live }}</ref> It is officially nicknamed "Park City" due to its 35 [[Park|public parks]], which take up 1,300 acres. Although none are headquartered within the city itself, more than a dozen [[Fortune 500]] companies are based in its metropolitan area. Bridgeport has been consistently ranked by various sites as among the 25 most ethnically and culturally diverse American cities.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.finder.com/most-diverse-cities-in-the-us |title=Most diverse cities in the United States |date=September 7, 2021 |access-date=December 13, 2022 |archive-date=December 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221204054800/https://www.finder.com/most-diverse-cities-in-the-us |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/multimedia/photos/the-25-most-diverse-cities-in-the-united-states/collection_a686531a-6c2e-5476-b96c-9af204acc0d0.html#3 |title=The 25 most diverse cities in the United States |date=February 10, 2021 |access-date=December 13, 2022 |archive-date=December 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221213132605/https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/multimedia/photos/the-25-most-diverse-cities-in-the-united-states/collection_a686531a-6c2e-5476-b96c-9af204acc0d0.html#3 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://hanfordsentinel.com/22-bridgeport-stamford-norwalk-connecticut/article_1c40e000-8205-5f28-a36b-694c404909e2.html |title=22.
